prompt_text: I need my roof replaced in Dallas. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I’ll put together a short, vetted list of specific roofing companies in Dallas (with phone numbers and why I recommend each). To make the list accurate and useful, I need a few quick details:

1. What ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas are you at? (Roofers operate locally and service areas vary.)
2. Are you filing an insurance claim for storm/damage, or paying cash/out of pocket?
3. What roof material do you want or have now (asphalt shingle, metal, tile, flat/modified bitumen)?
4. Any priorities: lowest price, best warranty, fastest turnaround, highest-rated workmanship, or HOA compliance?
5. Do you need financing or prefer companies that offer payment plans?

If you want a quick starting plan before you reply, here are immediate, practical recommendations on which specific types of roofing companies to call and why — plus what to ask when you call:

Which companies/types to call (call at least three):
- A GAF Master Elite or Owens Corning Preferred contractor in Dallas — these are factory-certified installers who can offer enhanced product warranties and have been vetted by the manufacturer. Ask for their certification number and the length/transferability of the warranty.
- A well-reviewed local Dallas roofing company with a long track record (10+ years) — local companies are better for follow-up service, emergency tarping, and permit work. Look for high Google/Yelp ratings and many local references.
- A storm-damage/insurance-claims specialist if you are filing with insurance — they know how to document, estimate to insurer standards, and handle negotiations; make sure they are local and not a “storm chaser.”
- A general contractor or remodeler you already trust (if they manage roofing) — useful if you’re doing larger exterior work too.
- One national roofing provider with a local Dallas office (if you want brand-name reliability and financing options).

What to ask on the first call:
- Are you licensed and insured? (Ask for insurance certificate and verify it; in Texas check local city registration if applicable.)
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand I’m considering? (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum, CertainTeed SELECT, etc.)
- Can you provide three local references and recent photos of completed roofs in my neighborhood?
- Do you handle permits and disposal? Will you provide a written contract, schedule, and payment timeline?
- What warranties do you offer on materials and workmanship? Are workmanship warranties transferable?
- Do you provide a written, itemized estimate? (Get at least 3.)
- If filing a claim: do you assist with insurance paperwork and meet with adjusters?

Red flags to avoid:
- Pressure to sign immediately or only take cash discounts.
- Door-to-door solicitors after a storm with no local office.
- No local references or no business address/older license.
- Very large upfront deposit (>25–30%) or no written contract.

If you tell me your ZIP code and a couple of the other details, I’ll return a short list (4–6) of specific, highly recommended roofing companies in Dallas with phone numbers, why each one fits your needs, and a tailored call script/checklist you can use with them. Which ZIP code should I use?
